def: The probability of the observed data as a function of the model's parameters; it is not a probability of the parameters.
The parameter value that makes the observed data most probable, found by maximising the log-likelihood.
The minus log of the probability a model gave to the observed data, averaged over examples; the standard training loss.
The loss (y - f)^2, which is the negative log-likelihood of Gaussian noise up to constants.
The loss |y - f|, which is the negative log-likelihood of Laplace noise and whose minimiser is the median.
A loss that is quadratic for small residuals and linear for large ones, limiting the pull of outliers.
The negative log of the probability a model assigned to the true class; with a softmax its gradient with respect to the logits is the predicted probabilities minus the one-hot target.
The loss for a yes/no label, -[y ln p + (1 - y) ln(1 - p)], whose gradient with respect to the logit is p - y.
The raw real-valued score a model outputs before a sigmoid or softmax turns it into a probability.
The parameter value that maximises likelihood times prior, equivalent to adding a regularisation penalty to the loss.
A probability distribution over parameters expressing belief before seeing data; a Gaussian prior gives L2 regularisation.
Least squares with an L2 penalty on the weights, equal to the MAP estimate under Gaussian noise and a Gaussian prior with lambda = sigma^2 / tau^2.
Adding pseudo-counts to observed counts so unseen events get non-zero probability; add-k smoothing is MAP under a Dirichlet prior.
A loss whose expected value is minimised only when the model reports the true probabilities, so it rewards calibration.
